5 steps to go live

  1. 1. Clone / create a Next.js project

    Start a new Next.js app (App Router + TypeScript) or clone your existing project. Install Prisma: npm install prisma @prisma/client.

  2. 2. Copy .env — keep secrets private

    Create a .env file in the project root. Never commit it. Use the template below and replace each value with your own.

  3. 3. Run npx prisma db push

    This creates the tables from your schema. Then run npx prisma generate to update the client.

  4. 4. Paste your API base URL

    Deploy the Next.js app (for example on Vercel) and paste its base URL below, e.g. https://your-app.vercel.app.

  5. 5. Test connection

    Use Test Connection to run a connection check, then wire the app to your real endpoints when you are ready.

.env template

DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/whacrm"
NEXTAUTH_SECRET="replace-with-a-long-random-secret"
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY="sk_test_..."
OWNER_EMAIL="you@yourbusiness.ng"

Keep DATABASE_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, OPENAI_API_KEY, PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY and OWNER_EMAIL out of screenshots and shared repos.

Prisma schema — starter models

model Lead {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  phone     String
  value     Int
  stage     String   @default("NEW")
  source    String
  note      String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
}

model Order {
  id       String @id @default(cuid())
  customer String
  items    String
  total    Int
  status   String @default("Pending")
  date     String
}

Add Product, Invoice, Campaign and Template models in the same file, then run npx prisma db push.
